'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Nyala]]
***Three people are killed and 30 others are injured in a [[shootout]] and subsequent [[Shell (projectile)|shelling]] at a hospital south of [[Nyala, Sudan|Nyala]], [[South Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202308150102.html (AllAfrica)]
***Clashes begin again in Nyala, with at least 43 people confirmed dead and dozens more injured. [https://allafrica.com/stories/202308150102.html (AllAfrica)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Two [[Palestinians]] combatants, including a 16-year old, are killed during a raid by [[Israeli Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] in [[Jericho]], in the occupied [[West Bank]]. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-west-bank-raid-9e552961589904c64caf30820cf1a831 (AP)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022–2023 Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***[[Russia]] launches a large-scale [[airstrike]] on [[Lviv]] and northwestern [[Volyn Oblast]], killing at least three [[civilian]]s and injuring more than a dozen others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-strikes-western-ukraine-large-scale-air-attack-officials-2023-08-15/ (Reuters)] 
**[[2022–2023 western Russia attacks]]
***[[Bryansk Oblast]] [[Governor of Bryansk Oblast|Governor]] [[Alexander Bogomaz]] says that [[Russian Ground Forces|Russian soldiers]] and [[Federal Security Service|security services]] stopped a Ukrainian [[sabotage]] group from infiltrating the border near the village of [[Kurkovichi]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2023/08/15/Russia-prevented-Ukrainian-saboteur-group-from-crossing-into-Bryansk-region-Governor (AFP via Al Arabiya)]
**[[Poland]] displays its weapons and defense systems at a [[military parade]] in [[Warsaw]] involving 2,000 troops, 200 vehicles and 100 aircraft. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-russia-war-defense-military-parade-bd9dd186f240370c28c49d47c56ac038 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2023 Brazil blackout]]
**[[Brazil]] is affected by a nationwide blackout, with all of the [[States of Brazil|states]] connected to the national energy system impacted. The state of [[Roraima]] is unaffected as it has its own energy system. The cause of the outage is still unknown. [https://brazilian.report/liveblog/politics-insider/2023/08/15/mystery-power-outage/ (The Brazilian Report)]
*[[Economy of China]]
**The [[China|Chinese]] [[National Bureau of Statistics of China|national statistics office]] announces that [[Retail|retail sales]] increased by 2.5% year on year in July, while [[industrial production]] increased by 3.7% and [[Unemployment in China|unemployment]] increased to 5.3%. However, further releases of statistics on age-specific data will be suspended. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/china-stops-releasing-youth-jobs-data-economic-figures-disappoint-3699656 (AFP via CNA)]
**The Chinese [[People's Bank of China|central bank]] lowers the medium-term lending facility rate, which is the interest rate on one-year loans to financial institutions, to 2.5%. [https://www.reuters.com/article/china-economy-rates/china-central-bank-cuts-rates-for-second-time-in-three-months-to-support-economy-idUSKBN2ZQ02R (Reuters)]
*[[Economy of Kenya]]
**[[Kenya]]'s [[government debt]] surges to a record [[Kenyan shilling|KSh]] 10.1 trillion ([[United States dollar|US$]]70.75 billion), surpassing its KSh 10 trillion [[debt limit]], attributed to [[external debt]] and [[Currency appreciation and depreciation|currency fluctuations]]. [[President of Kenya|President]] [[William Ruto]]'s response to the country's [[financial crisis]] has been met with months of [[civil disorder]]. [https://amp.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20230816-kenya-s-debt-rises-to-historic-high-treasury (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Sri Lankan economic crisis (2019–present)|Sri Lankan economic crisis]]
**[[Sri Lanka]] permits the importation of buses and trucks, reversing a part of its 2020 vehicle [[Import quota|import ban]] initiated due to [[Currency crisis|foreign exchange shortages]], while bans on cars, motorcycles, and [[three-wheeled motor scooter]]s persist pending improved [[Foreign exchange reserves|foreign reserves]]. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2023/08/943439/sri-lanka-lifts-import-ban-buses-trucks (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2023]]
**[[2023 Canadian wildfires]]
***A [[state of emergency]] is declared in [[Canada]]'s [[Northwest Territories]] as [[wildfire]]s spread closer to the territorial capital [[Yellowknife]]. The [[hamlet (place)|hamlet]] of [[Enterprise, Northwest Territories|Enterprise]], [[South Slave Region]], is almost completely destroyed due to the fires. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/northern-canadian-city-yellowknife-declares-emergency-due-wildfires-2023-08-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[2023 Hawaii wildfires]]
***In the [[United States]], [[Maui County, Hawaii|Maui County]] officials including [[Governor of Hawaii|Governor]] [[Josh Green (politician)|Josh Green]] say that the death toll of the wildfires have reached 106. [https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2023/08/15/biden-pledges-maui-visit-recovery-crews-continue-grim-search-remains-lahaina/ (''Hawaii News Now'')] [https://mauinow.com/2023/08/15/lahaina-wildfire-death-toll-rises-to-101/ (Maui Now)]
*[[2023 North India floods]]
**At least 65 people are killed and 20 others are missing after flooding and landslides in northern [[India]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230815-search-for-survivors-after-indian-floods-landslides-kill-58 (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2023 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Lan (2023)|Typhoon Lan]] makes landfall in western [[Japan]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/15/world/asia/typhoon-lan-japan.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Ecuadorian general election]]
**Pedro Briones, a local leader of the [[Citizen Revolution Movement]], is assassinated by gunmen in the northern province of [[Esmeraldas Province|Esmeraldas]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ecuador-crime-political-killing-election-villavicencio-14a5fd781e52d31855f3fc4e9711ff84 (AP)]
*Child welfare advocates in the United States file a [[Federal judiciary of the United States|federal lawsuit]] to require the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] to block imports of products containing [[Cocoa bean|cocoa]] [[Child labour|harvested by children]] in [[West Africa]], alleging that [[U.S. Customs and Border Protection|Customs and Border Protection]] and the [[United States Department of Homeland Security|Department of Homeland Security]] have ignored evidence of the existence of these imports. [https://apnews.com/article/child-labor-lawsuit-cocoa-human-rights-africa-f8d3c8c74d66b5745e1d77e1dfc178d0 (AP)]
*Former [[Malaysia]]n [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|prime minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] is acquitted by the [[High court (Malaysia)|high court]] of four [[corruption]] charges of obtaining bribes for his political party. [https://apnews.com/article/malaysia-corruption-former-prime-minister-muhyiddin-8bffff4e4fed2172a239427eb027dd9e (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**[[Spain women's national football team|Spain]] advances to the [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup final|final]] for the first time after defeating [[Sweden women's national football team|Sweden]] 2–1 in the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup knockout stage#Spain vs Sweden|semi-final]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/15/sports/soccer/womens-world-cup-spain-sweden.html (''The New York Times'')]
